scope.reason: The Express registration, the local middleware alias, the CommonJS constructor handler and the captured Mongo write are now linked: POST /benefits reaches db_write update on `users`. What remains unmodelled is the functional-role policy itself.

label.criterion: The upstream route file itself documents the missing admin guard as its function-level access-control vulnerability.
label.why: POST /benefits has isLoggedIn but not isAdmin; updateBenefits accepts req.body.userId and updates that user.

missCause: Functional-role policy is not structurally modelled: SPARDA can see that POST /benefits carries isLoggedIn and writes `users`, but it holds no evidence of which ROLE the route should require, so the absent isAdmin is not a provable obligation. The captured Mongo write provenance named by the previous cause IS now modelled. The route stays an explicit UNKNOWN.
